scope: Local Apple Silicon loopback probe only; no hosted deployment, fleet failover or full Rocci handler port.
method: Compile suspend.c with clang --target=wasm32 -O1 -nostdlib -Wl,--no-entry -Wl,--export=__stack_pointer -Wl,--export-memory suspend.c -o suspend.wasm.
Copy the existing actor counter dist/actor.wasm alongside the probe, matching its recorded artifact SHA-256.
Start celld dev with no_bundle and local persistence; GET the loopback origin; stop its process group and wait.
Run the same entry/config/Wasm through wrangler dev; GET its loopback origin; stop its process group and wait.
Keep logs outside the watched app directory. The initial Wrangler attempt reloaded repeatedly when its log was inside it.
limits: The JSPI workload is compiled C with a volatile stack frame and an asynchronous JavaScript timer, not a Roc hosted-effect ABI test.
The actual Roc module is tested separately through its existing synchronous import-free ABI.
Sequential calls only; unchanged C stack pointer and linear memory do not measure V8 JSPI stack allocation, whole-process memory or leak freedom.
Does not prove cancellation, concurrent suspended Roc invocations, outbound fetch, SSE parity or deployment recovery.
